subject: chemistry
title: Acids, alkalis and the pH scale
key_idea: Acids produce hydrogen ions, H⁺, in water. Alkalis produce hydroxide ions, OH⁻. The pH scale from 0 to 14 measures acidity: below 7 is acidic, 7 is neutral and above 7 is alkaline.

blocks.text: This section covers the ions that make a solution acidic or alkaline.

items.meaning: A substance that produces hydrogen ions, H⁺, in aqueous solution.
A substance whose aqueous solution contains hydroxide ions, OH⁻.
The reaction of an acid with an alkali to form a salt and water.

items: All acids produce **H⁺ ions** when they dissolve in water. Carbonic acid, H₂CO₃, is one example.
All alkalis contain **OH⁻ ions** in solution. Sodium hydroxide solution contains Na⁺ and OH⁻ ions.
The ion that makes a solution acidic is H⁺. The ion that makes it alkaline is OH⁻.

blocks.label: Neutralisation (ionic equation)
where: H⁺: hydrogen ion from the acid
OH⁻: hydroxide ion from the alkali

items: Acids produce H⁺ ions in water. Alkalis contain OH⁻ ions in solution.
In neutralisation, H⁺ ions react with OH⁻ ions to produce water.

blocks.text: The pH scale from 0 to 14 measures how acidic or alkaline a solution is.

items: Acidic solutions have a pH less than 7. A lower pH means a more acidic solution.
Alkaline solutions have a pH greater than 7. A higher pH means a more alkaline solution.
The higher the concentration of hydrogen ions in an acidic solution, the lower the pH.
The higher the concentration of hydroxide ions in an alkaline solution, the higher the pH.
Water and sodium chloride solution are neutral, with a pH of 7.

diagram.alt: Choose a pH to see the ions present and the colour of universal indicator.

options.label: pH 7
results: Equal numbers of H⁺ and OH⁻ ions

items: pH 7 is neutral, below 7 is acidic and above 7 is alkaline.
More H⁺ ions means a lower pH. More OH⁻ ions means a higher pH.

blocks.text: An indicator changes colour depending on whether a solution is acidic or alkaline.

items: Universal indicator, or any wide range indicator, gives a colour for every pH. It is green at pH 7.
A **pH probe** (pH meter) gives a more accurate pH than universal indicator paper.
Litmus only shows whether a solution is acidic or alkaline. It does not show how acidic or alkaline.

items.text: Use a glass rod to place a drop of the solution onto universal indicator paper.
Look at the colour produced on the paper.
Compare the colour with the pH chart to read the approximate pH.

items: Universal indicator shows the approximate pH. A pH probe is more accurate.
Litmus, methyl orange and phenolphthalein show only whether a solution is acidic or alkaline.

checks.q: Which ion do all acids produce in aqueous solution, and which ion do all alkaline solutions contain?
checks.a: Acids produce hydrogen ions, H⁺. Alkaline solutions contain hydroxide ions, OH⁻.

checks.q: What colour is universal indicator in potassium hydroxide solution? Give a reason.
checks.a: Blue or purple, because the solution is alkaline and contains hydroxide ions.

checks.q: Write the ionic equation for neutralisation.

exam_phrases: H+ (ions in acids); OH– (ions in alkalis)
universal indicator: green to red / orange / yellow in acid
(the solution is) alkaline; contains OH– ions

mistakes.wrong: Universal indicator turns green in nitric acid.
mistakes.right: Green is not accepted for an acid. Universal indicator is red in acid (orange or yellow also allowed). Green is neutral.

mistakes.wrong: A pH meter can be used to test if a solution is acidic.
mistakes.right: A pH meter is ignored here. Name an indicator and its result: universal (green to red, orange or yellow), litmus (turns red) or methyl orange (turns red).

mistakes.wrong: The pH at the start is 1 and at the end is 13 when sulfuric acid is added to sodium hydroxide.
mistakes.right: The alkali comes first, so the start is 12 to 14. With excess acid the end is 0 to 3. The values must be in this order.

worked_example.question:
Potassium hydroxide solution is produced when potassium reacts with water.

What is the colour of universal indicator when added to potassium hydroxide solution?

Give one reason for your answer.
answer_points: Reason: the solution is alkaline (it contains hydroxide ions, OH⁻).
worked_example.tip: One mark for the colour and one for the reason. Basic is also allowed for alkaline.

exam_phrases: (observe / look at) colour produced on (universal indicator) paper
litmus paper only shows if the solution is {acidic / alkaline}
does not show how acidic or alkaline the solution is

mistakes.wrong: Litmus paper is not suitable because it is not accurate.
mistakes.right: Not precise or accurate is ignored. Say litmus only shows whether a solution is acidic or alkaline, not how acidic or alkaline.

mistakes.wrong: Use an indicator to measure the pH.
mistakes.right: Indicator alone, or another named indicator, is not allowed. Use a pH meter or probe, or universal indicator or pH paper.

mistakes.wrong: Phenolphthalein goes from colourless to pink as the acid neutralises the alkali.
mistakes.right: It is pink or magenta in alkali and goes colourless as the alkali is neutralised. Both starting and final colours are needed.

worked_example.question:
A student investigated how the pH of a mixture changes as barium hydroxide is added to dilute hydrochloric acid.

Step 2: use a glass rod to place a drop of the acid onto a piece of universal indicator paper and record the pH.
Step 4: use the glass rod to place a drop of the mixture onto a new piece of universal indicator paper and record the pH again.

Describe how the pH of the mixture is determined when a drop of it is placed on the universal indicator paper.
answer_points: Observe (look at) the colour produced on the universal indicator paper.
Compare it to a pH chart (scale).
worked_example.tip: Both marks are for the method. Do not link a colour to acidity: that is ignored.

exam_phrases: hydrogen ion / H+ (makes a substance acidic)
universal indicator turns red in acid and green in neutral solutions
universal indicator is blue in alkali

mistakes.wrong: Universal indicator turns yellow in alkali.
mistakes.right: Universal indicator is blue (or purple) in alkali, not yellow.

mistakes.wrong: Solutions of alkalis contain H⁺ ions.
mistakes.right: Solutions of alkalis contain hydroxide ions, OH⁻. Hydrogen ions make a substance acidic.

mistakes.wrong: Universal indicator is blue when a solution is neutral.
mistakes.right: Universal indicator is green when a solution is neutral, at pH 7.

worked_example.question:
A student investigates a neutralisation reaction between an acid and an alkali.

The student adds universal indicator to the acid. The student predicts the colour change they think will happen when they add the alkali to the acid.

Colour of indicator before alkali is added: red
Colour of indicator when solution is neutral: green
Colour of indicator when too much alkali has been added: yellow

Do you agree with the student? Tick one box: the student is completely correct; the student is partly correct; the student is completely incorrect.

Explain your answer.
answer_points: Universal indicator turns red in acid and green in neutral solutions.
Universal indicator is blue (or purple) in alkali, not yellow.
worked_example.tip: Say what is right and what is wrong.
